messages:
raj: Quick RFC follow-up on precision profiles for serving (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit). Wanted to capture proposed interface, runtime fallbacks, and rollout checklist so we can move to an implementation spike.

maria: +1. can you outline how this differs from existing model variants? e.g., do we expose multiple model ids or a single model + precision hints?

raj: I propose a single model surface with an optional precision_profile field at the route/model config level. Runtime will map that to a kernel/quantized artifact. Benefits: single semantically stable model id, simpler rollouts. Drawbacks: extra runtime mapping layer and storage for multiple quantized shards.

sam: curious about the fallback cascade. do you mean try 4-bit, then int8, then fp16 if quality drops? how do we detect "quality drops" in production cheaply?

raj: exactly. cascade = attempt cheapest precision first, if inference-level checks fail, escalate to the next precision. For detection: two tiers
- fast signal: embedding cosine distance to baseline for vector routes, or token-level perplexity delta for generation routes (cheap stateless calc)
- slow confirm: offline evals on sampled traffic with full metrics (nll, BLEU/ROUGE, embedding drift)
If fast signal crosses threshold -> re-run that request at higher precision synchronously (fallback) and also start a deeper sample for auto-rollbacks.

anya: any runtime perf concerns? re-running requests for fallback could double latency for those edge cases.

raj: agree. plan is to only re-run when necessary and keep synchronous fallback limited (example: <= 0.1% of requests by tuning thresholds). Also we can offer async re-score for lower-priority features. We should expose SLA knobs per route: max_extra_latency_ms, fallback_mode (sync|async|none).

sam: kernel / hardware support is big: 4-bit + per-channel scales need specific CUDA kernels / graph. Do we expect our Dedicated/Private customers to have these kernels? fallback to int8/fp16 when missing?

raj: yes. runtime capability matrix will advertise supported precisions per deployment (hosted vs dedicated vs private). If hardware/kernel not available -> skip that precision in cascade.

maria: what about calibration? per-channel vs per-tensor, and calibration set size. we need a plan for both offline calibration and online adaptation.

raj: propose hybrid calibration:
1) offline static calibration during model onboarding (per-channel scales using representative dataset)
2) online micro-calibration: maintain running min/max and an EMA-based scale tweak for distribution shifts. Keep it conservative to avoid flipping scales often.

ci-bot: deploy-checklist bot: small note — ensure QA tests include deterministic seeds for quantized artifacts, and add embedding-drift asserts.

anya: how does API look? example config pls.

raj: here's a rough example config for route-level profile:

```
precision_profile:
  name: "latency-4bit"
  mode: "cascade"
  fallbacks:
    - precision: "int4"
      max_qlty_drop: 0.01    # fraction of baseline quality allowed
    - precision: "int8"
      max_qlty_drop: 0.001
    - precision: "fp16"
      max_qlty_drop: 0.0
  calibrate:
    method: "hybrid"
    offline_dataset: "onboarding-v1"
    online_sample_rate: 0.002
  runtime_policy:
    fallback_mode: "sync"
    max_extra_latency_ms: 200
    max_retries: 1
```

maria: looks good. for storage, do we store one quantized artifact per precision + shards? what's the expected extra storage overhead?

raj: naive approach: one artifact per precision. storage multiplier ~1x for fp16, ~0.5x for int8, ~0.25-0.3x for 4-bit (varies per format). We should support delta storage (store base fp16 + quantized deltas) to reduce duplication but that complicates runtime decoding.

sam: implementation notes for runtime:
- capability registry per node (supported precisions, kernel version)
- model manifest maps model->artifact per-precision
- decision engine that consults profile, capability, current SLO headroom, and recent quality stats
- fast-path: if profile==fixed_precision, call artifact directly. if cascade: attempt cheap variant with local quality check hook.

anya: rollout plan?

raj: propose staged rollout
1) unit/integration + instrumented sim on dev infra
2) canary: 1% traffic with synchronous fallback, watch fast signals + human eval on sampled requests
3) A/B: 10% vs control for 48-72h running full evals
4) gradual ramp to target (50-70%) then GA
Auto-rollback triggers: embedding drift > 0.02 cosine, per-token loss delta > 0.05 on sampled set, or user-reported regressions.

maria: we need a dashboard: per-route precision mix, fallback rate, extra-latency ppm, quality deltas, kernel compatibility heatmap.

raj: will draft a dashboard spec. Action items:
- sam: enumerate kernel/driver gaps across our fleet and partners
- maria: propose storage/layout options + cost model for artifacts
- anya: define API surface and SLA knobs
- raj: spike runtime decision engine + metrics plumbing

sam: noted. I'll start a matrix of supported kernels (cuquant, custom kernels, CPU fallback) and expected perf numbers.

anya: I'll draft API PR and include example curl/sdk usage.

ci-bot: Created issue INF-4627: "Precision profile rollout spike" (links: https://internal/inf/4627)

raj: thanks all. let's sync in next eng-ml sync; posting minutes to the RFC thread after I draft them.

maria: thanks — will add storage cost estimates to the issue.

sam: adding perf microbenchmarks to the issue as well.

anya: marking this for design review next Wed.

raj: end of thread.
